mainTopic: Does holiness lapse by itself? בר פדא's view, the delayed עולה, why a pledge to הקדש cannot be taken back, and a new question on בר פדא
overview: The גמרא is looking at a ברייתא about a person who makes an animal holy now and gives it a different kind of holiness that starts after thirty days. The ברייתא's two cases only make sense if one is about קדושת הגוף and the other is about קדושת דמים. That suggests even קדושת הגוף can disappear by itself. This seems to refute בר פדא, who said holiness never lapses by itself. רב פפא answers that בר פדא reads the ברייתא as speaking only of a case where the owner did not say 'from now it is a שלמים.' The animal still becomes an עולה after thirty days, just like a woman who is betrothed 'after thirty days.' The ruling teaches that even if the owner changes his mind, he cannot back out. Even according to the view that a woman can back out, הקדש is different, because words spoken to the Most High are as final as handing an item to a person. The amud ends with a story: two scholars sitting before a dozing רבי ירמיה begin a question built on בר פדא's view, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the ברייתא teaches two cases
steps.stepSummary: If one case is about קדושת הגוף and the other is about קדושת דמים, we understand why the תנא taught two cases. Otherwise we might think only קדושת דמים lapses by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: This explains why the תנא had to teach two cases. You might have thought that קדושת הגוף does not disappear by itself, while קדושת דמים does. So the תנא taught both, to show that both disappear by themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first half of an argument: 'It makes sense if one case is קדושת הגוף and the other is קדושת דמים.' This is setting up the next step, where the גמרא shows the other reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of the two cases teaches something new only if they are about different kinds of holiness. Without both cases, we would have assumed the stronger kind, קדושת הגוף, never lapses by itself. Teaching both shows that even it can lapse.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness of the body itself. The animal itself is holy for the מזבח.
Holiness of value. Only the animal's money value is holy.
It lapses or disappears.
For nothing, meaning by itself, with no פדיון or other action.
Two (here, two cases).
For it might enter your mind to say.

steps.confusionAlert: This step is only half of an argument. Its first half (בשלמא, 'it makes sense if...') came right before this section. Don't read it as a final ruling yet.

phrases.english: This is why it was necessary for the tanna
phrases.notes: This continues a line from just before: 'It makes sense if one case is קדושת הגוף and the other is קדושת דמים.'

phrases.english: to teach two cases.
For it might enter your mind to say:
Inherent holiness does not lapse by itself,
but holiness of value does lapse by itself.
Because of this, he taught two cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ דְּאִיצְטְרִיךְ לֵיהּ לְתַנָּא לְמִיתְנֵא תַּרְתֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'בשלמא' half of an argument begun before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the ברייתא's two cases deal with two different kinds of holiness.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא would have no reason to teach two cases otherwise.

steps.title: If both cases are about holiness of value, the second case is unnecessary
steps.stepSummary: If both cases were about קדושת דמים, the second case would be obvious. If strong holiness lapses into light holiness, then light holiness surely lapses into strong.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say both cases are about קדושת דמים, why teach two? If even strong holiness gives way to light holiness, do we really need to be told that light holiness gives way to strong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the other way of reading the ברייתא, that both cases are about קדושת דמים. Under that reading, one case would be pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going from עולה (stronger) to שלמים (lighter) is the harder case for holiness to lapse. If it lapses there, it obviously lapses going from lighter to stronger. So the extra case only makes sense if it teaches something about a different kind of holiness, קדושת הגוף.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both cases.
Severe or stronger holiness (here, an עולה).
Light or weaker holiness (here, a שלמים).
Now, used here to mean 'if even this is true...'
Does it need to be said? Meaning it is obvious.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's two cases only make sense if one is about קדושת הגוף. So the ברייתא seems to teach that even קדושת הגוף can lapse by itself.

phrases.english: But if you say
that both this case and that case are holiness of value,
why do I need to teach two cases?
Now, it can be said:
from strong holiness to light holiness, it lapses.
From light holiness to strong holiness,
does it need to be said?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ אִידֵּי וְאִידֵּי קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The 'אלא' half of the argument, showing the opposite reading fails.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that both cases in the ברייתא are about קדושת דמים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading, the second case is a simple קל וחומר from the first, so teaching it is pointless.

steps.title: Is this a refutation of בר פדא?
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא shows that even קדושת הגוף lapses by itself, it seems to refute בר פדא, who said holiness never lapses by itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of בר פדא, who said that holiness does not lapse by itself?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now uses the conclusion of the last two steps to challenge בר פדא's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא held that holiness does not simply disappear without an action like פדיון. The ברייתא, as just read, has holiness disappearing by itself when the thirty days arrive. That seems to contradict him directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It opens a suggested conclusion.
A refutation, a strong challenge from a source.

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of Bar Padda,
who said: Holiness does not lapse by itself?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the conclusion of steps 1 and 2 against בר פדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: בר פדא's rule that holiness does not lapse by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has even קדושת הגוף lapsing on its own after thirty days.

steps.title: רב פפא rereads the ברייתא for בר פדא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says בר פדא reads the ברייתא as: only if he did not say 'from now it's a שלמים' does it become an עולה after thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: בר פדא can answer you that this is what the ברייתא means. If the person did not say 'from now it is a שלמים,' then after thirty days it is an עולה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends בר פדא by explaining the ברייתא differently, so it no longer shows holiness lapsing by itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, the ברייתא's ruling 'after thirty days it is an עולה' applies only when no שלמים holiness was placed on the animal first. If he did say 'from now it is a שלמים,' that holiness takes hold and does not just disappear. So the ברייתא no longer contradicts בר פדא.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you, introducing a defense for someone.
This is what it means, introducing a rereading of a source.
From now.
A burnt-offering (stronger holiness).
A peace-offering (lighter holiness).

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא first seemed to prove that holiness can lapse by itself. רב פפא rereads it so that בר פדא's rule still stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common גמרא move: a source that seems to refute someone is reread to fit his opinion.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Bar Padda can say to you,
this is what it is saying:
If he did not say 'from now it is a peace-offering,'
then after thirty days it is a burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אָמַר לָךְ בַּר פְּדָא, הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against בר פדא raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the ברייתא so it refers to a different case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא teaches that שלמים holiness placed 'from now' lapses by itself after thirty days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks only of when he did not say 'from now it is a שלמים.' So no holiness lapses by itself, and בר פדא stands.

steps.title: Comparison to betrothal that starts after thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The delayed עולה works just like קידושין that take effect after thirty days, even if the money is gone by then.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is just like a man who says to a woman, 'Be betrothed to me after thirty days.' She becomes betrothed, even though the money was used up before then.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב פפא's reading with a familiar comparison. A holiness that starts later is like קידושין that start later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the קידושין case, the money is given now, but the betrothal only takes effect after thirty days. It still works even if the money no longer exists on day thirty. In the same way, the animal can become an עולה after thirty days based on what the owner said today.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like, a comparison to a known case
Be betrothed to me, the words of קִידּוּשִׁין
The money was used up and is gone

phrases.english: It is just like the case of
one who says to a woman:
"Be betrothed to me after thirty days,"
that she is betrothed
even though the money was used up.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב פפא's reading by showing that a delayed effect is a known legal pattern.
steps.raayaObject: A holiness can take effect after thirty days based on a statement made now.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The case of קידושין that take effect after thirty days, even when the money was used up.

steps.title: Isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we need to be taught that the animal becomes an עולה after thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ruling as too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owner said the animal would be an עולה after thirty days and nothing changed, of course it becomes one. So why would the ברייתא bother to say it?

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious, so why teach it?

phrases.english: It's obvious!
phrases.notes: What's obvious: if he never changed his mind, of course the animal becomes an עולה after thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the rule just explained needs to be taught at all.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the ruling that the animal becomes an עולה after thirty days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A delayed הקדש that nobody changed should obviously take effect, so teaching it seems pointless.

steps.title: The case is where he changed his mind
steps.stepSummary: The ruling is needed for a case where the owner tried to back out during the thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed where he retracted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ruling teaches something new. The owner tried to take back his words before day thirty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new point is that backing out does not help. Even though the holiness has not started yet, the animal still becomes an עולה after thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed for a special case
He changed his mind or retracted

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he retracted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling only covers an owner who never changed his mind, which is obvious.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling covers an owner who retracted within thirty days, and his retraction does not work.

steps.title: What about the view that a woman can retract?
steps.stepSummary: The comparison works only for the view that the woman cannot back out. For the view that she can, the comparison seems to fail.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well according to the one who says she cannot retract. But according to the one who says she can retract, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison to קידושין. There is a view that a woman can back out during the thirty days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the comparison is to קידושין, then by that view the owner of the animal should also be able to back out. That would go against the ruling that his retraction does not help.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well for one view
She can retract and cancel the betrothal
What can be said? A challenge that needs an answer

phrases.english: This works well for the one who says
she cannot retract.
But for the one who says she can retract,
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of step 5 now that step 7 says retraction does not help.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the delayed עולה and delayed קידושין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to the view that a woman can retract within thirty days, the comparison suggests the owner should also be able to retract.

steps.title: Words to Heaven are like a handover to a person
steps.stepSummary: Even if a woman can retract, הקדש is different. A statement to the Most High is as binding as physically handing an item to a regular person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says that there she can retract, here it is different. His statement to the Most High is like his handing over to an ordinary person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that הקדש is stronger than קידושין. Once he spoke to the Most High, he cannot take it back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a regular person, a deal is final once the item is handed over. With הקדש, speaking alone has that same final power. So even though the עולה status starts later, the owner is already locked in.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different
His spoken statement to the Most High, meaning הֶקְדֵּשׁ
His handing over an item to an ordinary person

steps.whatToRemember: A spoken pledge to הקדש is as final as handing something to a person. So even a delayed הקדש cannot be cancelled, even according to the view that a woman can back out of delayed קידושין.

phrases.english: Even according to the one who says
there she can retract,
here it is different
because his statement to the Most High
is like his handing over to an ordinary person.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הָתָם חוֹזֶרֶת הָכָא שָׁאנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by separating הקדש from קידושין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If a woman can retract from delayed קידושין, an owner should be able to retract from a delayed הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: הקדש is different because words to the Most High are as binding as a physical handover, so he cannot retract.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic rule of הקדש: speech alone makes it binding, much like a completed handover between people.

steps.title: Two scholars sit before a dozing רבי ירמיה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets the scene: רבי אבין and רב יצחק בר רבי are sitting before רבי ירמיה, who is dozing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבין and רב יצחק son of רבי sat before רבי ירמיה, and רבי ירמיה was dozing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a short story. It is setting up a discussion that two scholars are about to have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No legal point is made yet. The detail that רבי ירמיה is dozing is part of the scene, because the two students begin their discussion while he is half asleep.

keyTerms.meaning: sat (here: sat and learned)
before him, in his presence
dozing, half asleep

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Avin and Rav Yitzchak son of Rabbi sat
before Rabbi Yirmeya,
and Rabbi Yirmeya was dozing.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְתֵיב רַבִּי אָבִין וְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרַבִּי קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the finished comparison between הקדש and קידושין to a new story that will introduce a new question.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling. This is a narrative setup for the discussion that follows.

steps.title: Starting a question based on בר פדא's view
steps.stepSummary: The two scholars begin to ask a question according to בר פדא, who holds that consecrated items that are redeemed become holy again.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat and said: according to בר פדא, who said that if he redeems them they become holy again,
steps.whatsHappening: The scholars begin to state a question. First they lay down the opinion they are working with, which is בר פדא's view. The actual question comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר פדא holds that after these items are redeemed, they become holy again. The scholars use this view as the starting point for their question. This line only states that starting point, so the learner should expect the question itself to come next.

keyTerms.meaning: he redeemed them (bought them out of holiness)
they become holy again

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence is not finished here. Do not look for the answer or even the full question yet; this line only says whose opinion the question is built on.

phrases.english: they sat and said:
According to bar Padda, who said
if he redeems them, they become consecrated again,
phrases.notes: "Them" means the holy items from בר פדא's ruling discussed earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתְבִי וְקָאָמְרִי לְבַר פְּדָא דְּאָמַר פְּדָאָן חוֹזְרוֹת וְקוֹדְשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The scene from step 10 now produces the scholars' discussion, which opens with the view of בר פדא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The question is not finished yet. So far the scholars have only said it is built on בר פדא's view that redeemed items become holy again.
